messages:
devin: heads-up — CI turned red on my feature branch feature/pipeline-refactor after merging main. failing on the integration shard: `tests/integration/test_pipeline.py::test_transform_shard` (shard 3). not sure if regressed by main or my change. stack snippet below

ci-bot: build 8842 • linux-x86-64 • shard 3 
FAIL tests/integration/test_pipeline.py::test_transform_shard - AssertionError: expected 42 != 0
Full log: https://ci.redwood.example/8842/3

sarah: can you paste the minimal failing output? is it deterministic on rerun? :thinking:

devin: paste from the failure: 
```
E   AssertionError: expected 42 != 0
.../transformer/pipeline.py:213 in process_shard
KeyError: 'last_checkpoint'
```
Only seeing this on shard 3 (note: other shards passed). I tried a local docker run and couldn't repro yet.

matt: hmm that KeyError smells like a race in the checkpoint lookup we patched last week in main. i touched that area in #4321 (kernel selection + cache invalidation).

julie: @devin can you kick a rerun for just shard 3? sometimes flakes hide other issues. if it fails again we'll bisect.

devin: done: /rerun shard=3 — queued (build 8843)

ci-bot: rerun queued for build 8843 • linux-x86-64 • shard 3

ci-bot: build 8843 • shard 3 • FAILURE (same trace)

kevin: ok reproducible in CI. @sarah want to bisect? if it's between main and your branch we can git-bisect main..HEAD but might be quicker to try reverting the cache invalidation change in #4321.

sarah: i'll start a quick bisect tomorrow morning. can someone post the exact bisect command they use for these integration shards? want to avoid flapping the CI too much.

matt: typical steps i use: 
```
git fetch origin
git checkout feature/pipeline-refactor
git bisect start HEAD origin/main
# run the integration test (local docker) — this script mirrors CI shard 3
scripts/ci/run_integration_shard.sh --shard 3
# git bisect good/bad as appropriate
```
If the local script is slow, do `pytest tests/integration/test_pipeline.py::test_transform_shard -q -k shard3` inside the same container image.

julie: also check env var `REDWOOD_CACHE_STRICT=true` — main added a change that makes cache lookups strict and will KeyError if missing. maybe your branch expects fallback behavior.

devin: ahhhhh that could be it. i didn't account for the strict flag. i can try a quick local run with REDWOOD_CACHE_STRICT=true.

sarah: for coordination: i'll own the bisect and report back. @matt can you open a revert PR for #4321 if bisect points there? quicker rollback helps prod customers.

matt: yep can cut a revert PR fast if needed. also i'll run the local shard script now to see if i can reproduce.

kevin: tagging release lead — we should avoid a long outage but this is infra test failing not prod. still want to move fast. :shipit:

devin: local with REDWOOD_CACHE_STRICT=true reproduces the KeyError. narrowing it down now. thanks all.

sarah: update — started bisect (on CI clone to avoid spamming main). first few steps inconclusive, bisecting deeper. i'll post the commit id when found.

matt: if bisect lands on my change i’ll revert + add a fallback. if it's on main earlier i can patch to maintain compatibility.

julie: if anyone needs a quick hotfix for the tests to unblock merges, we can add a temporary test skip with TODO referencing this thread. prefer bisect first though.

kevin: thanks team. assigning follow-ups: sarah = bisect + report, matt = potential revert/patch, devin = add strict-env local repro steps in the PR. ping here when you have the commit.
